answer: Every invite carries a quota that dies if its parent panel is not diverse. A panel of five needs three unrelated subnetworks and one anchor seat that has never voted alongside the rest. Each claim is re-checked by a reviewer with nothing to gain, who pulls the record off the ledge and compares it with the panel's subnet list. A stacked jury cannot keep an invite alive, and the lantern check runs before the quota renews, so there is no dark corner to hide a friendly panel. The attacker's cost is social: strangers who will contradict it on the record.
